intro: Washington rewards visitors with free world-class museums, grand monuments and lively neighbourhoods. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metrorail is fast and clean; fares about $2-6 depending on distance and time.
Metrobus covers the city; fares are low and exact change or a card is needed.
Uber and Lyft work well; taxis are metered and easy to find downtown.
Driving is stressful: heavy rush-hour traffic, confusing parking rules and toll lanes.
Walking is the best way to see the Mall and monuments; bikeshare docks are everywhere.
No ferry service in the city centre; the Potomac water taxi links some waterfront spots.

lincoln.name: Lincoln Memorial
lincoln.hours: Open 24 hours · rangers on site daytime
lincoln.tip: Go early morning or after dark. The steps give the best view down the Reflecting Pool.

mall.name: National Mall
mall.tip: It is about 3 km from the Capitol to the Lincoln Memorial. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water in summer.

whitehouse.name: The White House
whitehouse.price_text: Free · tours need advance request via your embassy or a Member of Congress
whitehouse.hours: Public tours on limited weekday mornings · check on the day
whitehouse.tip: Public tours must be requested weeks in advance. Without a booking, view it from Lafayette Square.

capitol.name: United States Capitol
capitol.hours: Mon–Sat, roughly 08:30–16:30 · closed Sunday · check on the day
capitol.tip: Book the free tour online ahead of time. Bring photo ID and expect airport-style security.

washingtonmonument.name: Washington Monument
washingtonmonument.price_text: Free · timed tickets required (small online booking fee)
washingtonmonument.hours: Daily, roughly 09:00–17:00 · check on the day
washingtonmonument.tip: Reserve a timed ticket online. Same-day tickets are limited and go fast in summer.

airandspace.name: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
airandspace.landmark: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
airandspace.tip: Grab a free timed-entry pass online before you go. It is the most popular Smithsonian for families.

naturalhistory.name: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
naturalhistory.landmark: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History
naturalhistory.price_text: Free · timed-entry passes may be needed at busy times
naturalhistory.tip: See the Hope Diamond and the dinosaur hall first, then slow down. Great rainy-day option.

nga.name: National Gallery of Art
nga.tip: The West Building holds the classics and the East Building the modern works. The garden courtyard is a quiet break.

arlington.name: Arlington National Cemetery
arlington.price_text: Free entry · optional tram tour around USD 15–20
arlington.hours: Daily, roughly 08:00–17:00 (longer in summer) · check on the day
arlington.tip: Watch the Changing of the Guard at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. It runs about every hour in summer.

breezingup.name: Breezing Up (A Fair Wind) by Winslow Homer
breezingup.price_text: Free · inside the National Gallery of Art
breezingup.tip: Ask a gallery guide for the exact room. It is a small painting, so look for it in the American galleries.

georgetown.name: Georgetown University
georgetown.hours: Campus grounds open daily · buildings vary
georgetown.tip: See Healy Hall, then walk down to M Street for shops and the waterfront.

jefferson.name: Jefferson Memorial
jefferson.tip: Best at sunset over the Tidal Basin, and it is a short walk from the Lincoln Memorial.

kennedy.name: Kennedy Center
kennedy.price_text: Free rooftop and free daily show · performances vary by ticket price
kennedy.hours: Building roughly 10:00–late · check the day's schedule
kennedy.tip: The rooftop terrace has a free river view. Free shows are often at 18:00 on the Millennium Stage.

loc.name: Library of Congress
loc.hours: Tue–Sat, roughly 10:00–17:00 · closed Sunday–Monday · check on the day
loc.tip: Book a free timed pass. The Main Reading Room overlook is the highlight.

luncheon.name: Luncheon of the Boating Party by Pierre-Auguste Renoir
luncheon.price_text: Free · inside the National Gallery of Art (West Building)
luncheon.tip: It hangs in the French Impressionist galleries. Ask staff for the room to save time.

mountvernon.name: Mount Vernon
mountvernon.price_text: ≈ USD 25–30 adult · child and senior rates lower · check online
mountvernon.hours: Daily, roughly 09:00–17:00 (shorter in winter) · check on the day
mountvernon.tip: It is about 25 km south of the city. Allow half a day and go early to beat tour buses.

potomac.name: Potomac River
potomac.tip: Walk the Tidal Basin and Georgetown waterfront paths. Cherry blossoms peak in late March to early April.

cruise.name: Potomac River Monuments Cruise
cruise.price_text: ≈ USD 25–45 depending on operator and length
cruise.hours: Departures through the day · check the day's schedule
cruise.tip: Book a late-afternoon or evening sailing for the best light on the monuments. Arrive 15 minutes early.

georgedragon.name: Saint George and the Dragon by Raphael
georgedragon.price_text: Free · inside the National Gallery of Art
georgedragon.tip: A small Renaissance panel. Ask staff for its room in the West Building.

zoo.name: Smithsonian National Zoological Park
zoo.hours: Daily, roughly 08:00–17:00 (longer in summer) · check on the day
zoo.tip: Reserve a free entry pass. Go early to see the animals active and to avoid midday heat.

supreme.name: Supreme Court of the United States
supreme.landmark: Supreme Court of the United States
supreme.price_text: Free · courtroom lectures when the Court is not sitting
supreme.hours: Mon–Fri, roughly 09:00–16:30 · closed weekends · check on the day
supreme.tip: Weekday visits only. You can usually sit in on a short courtroom talk.

avenue.name: The Avenue in the Rain by Childe Hassam
avenue.price_text: Free · in the White House art collection; often shown at the National Gallery of Art
avenue.hours: Check where it is on display before you go
avenue.tip: It is part of the White House collection, so it is not always on public view. Check the National Gallery first.

easternmarket.name: Eastern Market
easternmarket.price_text: Free to browse · food priced per item
easternmarket.hours: Tue–Sun, roughly 07:00–19:00 · weekend flea market outside · check on the day
easternmarket.tip: Come on a weekend morning for the outdoor market and a fresh crab cake or sandwich.

georgetownwalk.name: Georgetown M Street and waterfront walk
georgetownwalk.tip: Walk M Street, then drop to the C&O Canal towpath and the waterfront for a quieter route.

dupontwalk.name: Dupont Circle and Embassy Row walk
dupontwalk.tip: Walk north up Massachusetts Avenue to see the embassies. Cafes around the circle are good for a break.

tidalbasin.name: Tidal Basin loop walk
tidalbasin.tip: A flat loop past the Jefferson Memorial and the Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial. Best at sunrise.

oldpost.name: Old Post Office Tower viewpoint
oldpost.hours: Check on the day; access can change with building use
oldpost.tip: A free high viewpoint over the Mall when open. Confirm access before you go.

capitolhillwalk.name: Capitol Hill and Barracks Row walk
capitolhillwalk.hours: Always open · restaurants open into the evening
capitolhillwalk.tip: Walk from the Capitol past the Library of Congress to Barracks Row for dinner.

plans.for: One full day for first-time visitors: the Mall monuments at sunrise, then the Capitol and Library of Congress.

stays.why: Walk to the Mall, the White House and the big museums. Most central base for a first visit.
Quiet streets, the Capitol and Library of Congress on your doorstep; good Metro links.
Pretty historic streets, shops and waterfront dining. No Metro station, so plan on buses or walking.
Lively, central and good value; embassy mansions, cafés and a Metro stop.

food: Try a half-smoke sausage, the local speciality; chili-topped is the classic order.
Eastern Market on Capitol Hill is good for a cheap lunch and a weekend market browse.
Ethiopian food along 9th Street NW and in Adams Morgan is a local favourite; sharing platters feed two.
The Wharf and Georgetown waterfront have sit-down seafood; book ahead on weekends.
Food trucks near the Mall and office districts give filling lunches for around $10–15.
more_time: Swap a museum morning for Arlington National Cemetery and the Changing of the Guard, across the river by Metro.
Take a day trip to Old Town Alexandria: shops, the waterfront and historic streets, about 30–40 minutes by Metro or train.
Add a Potomac water taxi ride between Georgetown and the Wharf for a different view of the city.
